description: Stellar Minds ✨ is a team passionate about space exploration, scientific discovery, and storytelling. We aim to research NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars using reliable sources and creative communication. We value curiosity, teamwork, and scientific accuracy. Our interests include space science, research, writing, drawing, graphic design, and multimedia.
summary:
Project Summary – Abandoned but Not Forgotten

Our project is about NASA's unsuccessful and successful space missions and the equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. We want to show that even if some equipment is left behind, it does not mean it has become useless.

Maybe NASA left these machines and tools for a reason, and one day they could help us again. In the future, if humans ever need to live beyond Earth, we might be able to use, repair, or reconnect with some of this equipment to support our survival and exploration.

We also believe that these forgotten machines may help future scientists discover new things about the Moon, Mars, and space. What we leave behind today could become something very important tomorrow.

Our message is simple: Just because something is abandoned doesn't mean its story is over.
details: Our project, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten,” explores the equipment and technology left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. It tells the stories of these discarded objects, explaining their original purposes, how they contributed to scientific discoveries, and why they remain important even after completing their missions. The project works through research-based storytelling and visual presentation. It highlights examples of space mission hardware, including lunar mission equipment and the parachute and backshell debris from NASA's Perseverance rover landing on Mars. The main benefit of this project is to help people understand that space exploration is not only about the discoveries we bring back but also about the technology and traces we leave behind. Our intended impact is to increase public awareness, encourage curiosity about planetary exploration, and inspire students to learn more about space science and engineering. We used NASA's publicly available information and images for research, along with Microsoft PowerPoint for designing and presenting our project. The project does not require custom coding or specialised hardware. Its creativity lies in transforming scientific information into an engaging storytelling experience. Instead of simply listing discarded equipment, we present these objects as important parts of humanity's journey into space. While developing the project, we considered scientific accuracy, reliable NASA sources, educational value, visual clarity, and accessibility for students and general audiences. Our message is simple: Even when a mission moves forward, the objects it leaves behind continue to tell its story.
